punchline: The women were told radium paint was harmless and shaped their brushes with their lips, while the company's chemists used tongs.
thirty_sec: At a New Jersey factory, young women painted watch dials with glowing radium paint, pointing the brush with their lips and told it was harmless, while the chemists used tongs and screens. Many fell ill. Grace Fryer found a lawyer and five women sued, settling in 1928.
